sources.title: Andrey V. Poliakov, Svetlana V. Svyatko and Nadezhda F. Stepanova, A Review of the Radiocarbon Dates for the Afanasyevo Culture (2019; online 2018)
sources.note: Publisher abstract directly checked. DOI 10.1017/RDC.2018.70. Short chronology describes a dated core, not exhaustive bounds for all sites.

sources.title: William Honeychurch and colleagues, The earliest herders of East Asia: Examining Afanasievo entry to Central Mongolia (2021)
sources.note: Original publisher abstract and introduction indexed in search; direct fetch 403. Migration and diffusion, introduction of livestock and metallurgy, and indigenous contributions explicitly distinguished.

sources.title: Alexey A. Tishkin, Taylor Hermes and Sergei P. Grushin, Nizhnyaya Sooru Settlement in Central Altai (2021)
sources.note: Original English article PDF directly read, particularly pp. 125, 129, 131 and concluding chronology/metallurgy discussion. Recounts small 1994 excavations; identifies ongoing erosion in 2019-2020.

sources.title: Taylor R. Hermes and colleagues, Mitochondrial DNA of domesticated sheep confirms pastoralist component of Afanasievo subsistence economy (2020)
sources.note: Original paper on institute repository directly read; DOI 10.1016/j.ara.2020.100232. Five tested teeth identified as domestic sheep, two radiocarbon dated; broad 3300-2900 BCE wording from authors.

sources.title: Taylor R. Hermes, Svetlana V. Shnaider and colleagues, Revisiting the emergence of pastoralism in the Altai Mountains (2021)
sources.note: Original six-page paper directly read. DOI 10.1016/j.ara.2021.100281. Introduction, Ust-Biyke-I and Eneolithic transitions pp. 1-3, and Nizhnyaya Sooru research pp. 5-6. Contact framed as a research problem, not a demonstrated universal exchange system.

sources.title: Alicia R. Ventresca Miller and colleagues, The spread of herds and horses into the Altai (2022)
sources.note: Original PLOS study directly read. Archaeological sites sampled, identified proteins and Transitioning to pastoral lifeways. Early sheep milk distinguished from much later horse dairying.

sources.title: Svetlana V. Svyatko and colleagues, Stable isotope palaeodietary analysis of the Early Bronze Age Afanasyevo Culture in the Altai Mountains (2017)
sources.note: University-hosted original paper directly read; DOI 10.1016/j.jasrep.2017.05.023. Abstract and Overall dietary assessment: regionally different fish use, protein-rich diet and qualified sex difference.

sources.title: Dairy-millet synergy underpinned subsistence adaptation to Inner Asian mountains from 2900 BCE (2026)
sources.note: Original paper directly read. Narensu exact coordinates 45.570 N, 83.558 E fall south of imported Afanasevo polygon. Radiocarbon modelling, cattle vertebra, isotope-based millet inference and later Khemceg/Andronovo sequence checked.

sources.title: Vagheesh M. Narasimhan and colleagues, The Formation of Human Populations in South and Central Asia, Supplementary Materials (2019)
sources.note: Harvard-hosted original supplement directly unavailable, exact indexed original query reproduced: site:reich.hms.harvard.edu "I6711" "son" "RISE511". Afanasieva Gora relatedness summary confirms mother RISE511, son I6711, brother I3387. Other family entries contain sex/ID inconsistencies and are not used.

sources.title: Simon Rasmussen and colleagues, Early Divergent Strains of Yersinia pestis in Eurasia 5,000 Years Ago (2015)
sources.note: Original Cell paper at Technical University of Denmark directly read; Table 1 identifies two Afanasievo Gora samples and calibrated ranges. Infection evidence not turned into epidemic-size, treatment or collapse claim. No categorical claim that all early flea transmission was impossible.

sources.title: Choongwon Jeong and colleagues, A Dynamic 6,000-Year Genetic History of Eurasia’s Eastern Steppe (2020)
sources.note: Original article indexed text checked for Afanasievo archaeological sites, Shatar Chuluu architecture and material; direct PMC request met reCAPTCHA. No claim that every burial contained every artifact.

sources.title: Rasmus G. Bjørn, Indo-European loanwords and exchange in Bronze Age Central and East Asia (2022)
sources.note: Direct article previously read and original indexed witness rechecked: Early archaeological cultures states Afanasievo has no written artifacts. Relationship to Tocharian is a hypothesis. Same work already contributes 113 words to new Andronovo packet; combined budget explicitly checked.

proposedOverrides.name: Afanasevo
proposedOverrides.summary: Early herding communities and changing regional traditions; the imported span extends beyond the principal archaeological dates.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: New archaeological-horizon card only; Yamnaya, Andronovo and Sintashta remain distinct.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Nearly identical Polygons in hb/borders/world-bc3000.json (-3000 to -2000) and world-bc2000.json (-2000 to -1500); bbox approximately [74.381,46.904,101.915,56.270]. Repeated envelope is not a state boundary. Narensu at 45.570 N is outside to the south; public passage states this.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Early regional evidence partly precedes 3000 BCE and most core burial sequences end well before 1500 BCE. Imported span retained only as map_coverage. Afanasievo spelling is treated as same conventional archaeological label, not a separate nation.
batchIdentityNotes.relationships: Yamnaya is a linked western archaeological/genetic population, not an alias or proven shared political state. Okunev follows regionally in Minusinsk. Andronovo and Sintashta belong to later, distinct archaeological discussions.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceReuse: Bjørn language work also in Andronovo packet; combined work budget checked separately even if not yet integrated.
